Artist / Educator / Maker

About James Jared Taylor

An artist’s practice shaped by observation, experiment, craftsmanship, and the belief that painting and sculpture speak a common language.

Biography

A life in the arts.

James Jared Taylor is an American artist whose practice moves between painting and sculpture. Trained in sculpture and metal fabrication, he brings a construction-minded approach to images, materials, and space. After decades of living and teaching in Southern California, he relocated to Oregon in 2025, where he continues to work in both visual art and music.

Originally from Cincinnati, Ohio, Taylor earned a BFA from the Kansas City Art Institute in 1981 and an MFA from Rutgers University’s Mason Gross School of the Arts in 1986. He apprenticed and worked at the Johnson Atelier, developing expertise in bronze casting and metal fabrication.

His work has appeared in solo and group exhibitions across the United States and is represented in public, private, and corporate collections. An ACI Artists and Writers Residency in Corciano, Italy in 2022 further informed an evolving studio practice.

Alongside making art, Taylor spent 32 years as an educator, teaching visual art and art history at secondary and college levels before retiring from teaching in 2020.

Artist statement

In two dimensions.
In three dimensions.

I see no difference between them since they are derived from the same sources. The work simply becomes a brief record of action, improvisation, intent, combined with the constant impulse to build or construct in two or three-dimensional space.

Rather than work toward a fixed result, the studio remains a place for trial and error, evolution, and discovery.
